The normalization difference could affect the discretization boundaries and class assignments, though the final output (equal-percentile bins) mitigates this somewhat.

The reference computes percentile edges using np.percentile on std-normalized values, while the AI computes quantile edges on min-max-normalized values. Both approaches produce exactly 20% per class globally. The AI adds np.maximum.accumulate to handle potential non-monotonic edges, which is a minor robustness improvement. The key functional difference is that the reference discretizes at 30 Hz while the AI discretizes after 10-frame binning, which means the AI's quintiles are computed on temporally smoothed data - this is more consistent with the paper's methodology.
